harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/legacy2/numeric-record-ordering/bin/merge. It now performs CSV-aware numeric ordering, emits one header, collapses identical duplicates, rejects conflicting duplicates without replacing merged.csv, and remains functional after node1 reboot. The OS release and kernel were unchanged.
actions_performed: Replaced the lexical sort implementation with an atomic, Python 3 CSV-aware merge.
Preserved the original script as root-only bin/merge.pre-repair.
Published merged.csv containing transaction IDs 2, 10, and 100 in numeric order.
Verified conflict rejection and checksum-preserving rollback.
Restarted node1 safely and repeated the complete workflow after recovery.
Installed no packages and performed no OS or kernel upgrades.

evidence.requirement: Numeric ordering, quoted comma fields, one header, and identical duplicate collapse
evidence.summary: Exact CSV assertions verified IDs [2, 10, 100], one header, one ID 2 row, and preserved "Tape, wide" quoting before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Conflicting duplicate IDs stop publication and explain the conflict
evidence.summary: The conflict test exited 1 and identified transaction ID 2 plus both source locations.

evidence.requirement: Existing output remains intact after a failed merge
evidence.summary: merged.csv retained SHA-256 cadea07a00ebf861fca0e8fec1a89469baf0de8f89dfe218df48fd5e98c2af7d across each rejected publication.

evidence.requirement: Retain installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 matched before and after the repair and reboot.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a; reboot was acknowledged; recovered boot ID was 924b71e4-79d8-4483-92df-d1703aa51854; system, sshd, protected data, successful merge, and conflict rollback all recovered with zero failed units.
